text:
sasha: Heads up — support ticket from Acme Corp hitting 401s on Dedicated in their VPC behind our customer LB. Happens ~1/20 requests, but only when they send the opaque JWT in a cookie instead of an Authorization header. Repro below.

sasha: Repro steps: 1) vpc-dedicated, attach their LB (nginx -> envoy), 2) set cookie 'session_jwt' with opaque token, 3) curl via LB IP: `curl -v -b 'session_jwt=eyJhbGci...' https://api.internal.redwood/acme/model` — sometimes returns 200, more often 401 with:
```
HTTP/2 401
content-type: application/json
{"error":"unauthorized","reason":"invalid_token_claims"}
```

sasha: When they switch to header `Authorization: Bearer <token>` everything is stable. They claim LB is configured to forward cookies->headers for upstream, but suspect header trimming somewhere in path.

priya: Thanks — assigning to eng-runtime + infra. Do we have any recent changes in our gateway that could cause opaque cookie parsing to fail? :thinking:

matt: Not in runtime code. We don't parse cookies ourselves — we accept Authorization header or opaque token from upstream header `x-rdwd-auth` (custom). If their LB translates cookie->Authorization it should be fine. What does their LB config look like?

eli: From the support bundle they sent (attached), their nginx -> envoy uses this small lua snippet to rewrite cookie to header: `ngx.req.set_header("Authorization", "Bearer " .. cookie_session)`; envoy then has `forward_client_cert_details: SANITIZE_SET` + a custom listener that strips some headers for privacy. Could be sanitizer dropping Authorization on certain requests.

matt: Hmm. We recently added a conservative policy in our dedicated edge proxy to drop `Authorization` when the connection is from an internal IP range to avoid accidental credential forwarding. That should only apply to requests missing `x-rdwd-internal` header. If LB sometimes sends that header and sometimes not, it could flip behavior.

priya: Can we get a clear repro client-side? Sasha, can you run a quick loop and log raw request/response at the LB and at our gateway (we have debug logs)? Eg:
```
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -b 'session_jwt=TOKEN' https://lb.acme.example/model; done
```
And tail our dedicated edge debug: `rdwd-edge -log debug -filter auth`

sasha: Running now. Initial run: of 50 requests: 39 -> 401, 11 -> 200. At LB logs I see Authorization header present on every upstream request (nginx set it). At our edge debug stream I see 401s with this line repeated: `auth: missing header after sanitize` and sometimes `auth: header accepted`.

matt: That aligns with sanitizer heuristics flipping. Could be a race with connection reuse: if nginx reuses a keepalive connection without setting Authorization on the new request (depending on how lua sets headers), Envoy's `strip_cookie_headers` maybe clears it on connection-level. Do we have a known issue?
\
eli: We had an Envoy filter bug where per-connection header state persisted across requests when Lua modified headers, specifically when `preserve_external_request_headers` was false. Patch in 1765000xxx fixed most cases but didn't cover cookie->header rewrite race.

priya: Customer is on an older nginx build. Could be that their lua runs in a phase that doesn't set header on internal subrequests reliably. Workarounds?

matt: Short-term: ask them to set `Connection: close` on client or disable keepalive from LB to upstream. Also suggest they set the header via nginx `proxy_set_header Authorization "Bearer $cookie_session";` rather than lua, which is executed per request consistently.

sasha: I asked them to try `proxy_set_header` and also to disable keepalive between nginx and envoy. They tried proxy_set_header and report immediate improvement — 50/50 -> 50/50? Sorry, scratch that — after switching to `proxy_set_header` we got 50/50 in first run, but when they also disabled keepalive it became 50/50? Wait confusing — attaching updated logs.

infra-bot: deploy-notify: canary of edge sanitizer v2 rolled 2026-01-12 03:12 UTC to dedicated fleets in us-west-2, eu-west-1.

matt: @infra-bot that canary might be the change. Canary note shows sanitizer v2 has stricter per-connection trimming. We need to correlate deployment time with customer error onset. Sasha, when did Acme start seeing this?

sasha: Support ticket first reported 2026-01-13 09:10 UTC, consistent with canary.

eli: Ok here's a quick patch we can try on our side: relax sanitizer to preserve Authorization when `x-rdwd-internal` or when there's `x-forwarded-for` present from LB. I'll open a fast patch CHERRY-PICK to the canary config and roll to affected fleets. Also propose a longer-term fix: make header sanitization per-request not per-connection.

matt: Agree. Also add telemetry counter `auth.sanitize.dropped_authorization` with label `connection_id` so we can link to LB logs by conn id.

priya: Communicated plan to customer: 1) temporary: ask LB/nginx -> use `proxy_set_header` and or disable keepalive, 2) we'll attempt hotfix roll to relax sanitizer, 3) follow up with perf/safety review. Customer is OK to try config changes while we test.

sasha: After we rolled the relaxed sanitizer to the affected fleet subset (eu-west-1 dedicated nodes for Acme), they reran loop: 48/50 -> 200, 2/50 -> 401. Huge improvement. They accepted as mitigation.

matt: Filing GH issue: runtime#4321 "auth sanitizer connection-level header drop for cookie->header rewrites" with repro, logs, and suggested fix. Will include customer repro script and LB/nginx snippet.

eli: We'll schedule the full fix for next sprint: convert sanitizer to be request-scoped, add tests for lua vs proxy_set_header cases, and include telemetry.

priya: Marking ticket P1 -> P2 since mitigation in place.

sasha: Closing loop with customer and documenting recommended LB config snippet in our Dedicated onboarding guide: `proxy_set_header Authorization "Bearer $cookie_session"; proxy_http_version 1.1; keepalive_timeout 0;`

sasha: Thanks all. Adding follow-up tasks to eng-runtime backlog. :thumbsup:
